summary: Pheniramine (as pheniramine maleate) is a first-generation alkylamine antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors to relieve allergic symptoms such as rhinitis, urticaria, and itching, and is used in injectable form for acute allergic and anaphylactic reactions and as an antiemetic/antivertigo agent. It is sedating and anticholinergic. It is widely available outside the US (often in combination cough/cold and ophthalmic products) and is not independently FDA-approved as a systemic single agent.

moa: Pheniramine is a competitive antagonist at peripheral and central histamine H1 receptors, blocking the effects of histamine released in allergic reactions (vasodilation, increased capillary permeability, itching). As a first-generation agent it crosses the blood-brain barrier (causing sedation) and has anticholinergic, antiemetic, and mild local anaesthetic properties.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to pheniramine or other antihistamines
relative: Prostatic hypertrophy / bladder neck obstruction / urinary retention
monitor: Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, blurred vision)

preg: Use only if clearly necessary. First-generation antihistamines are generally avoided near term because of possible neonatal effects (irritability, anticholinergic symptoms). Discuss with a clinician.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding; antihistamines may be excreted in milk, can reduce milk supply, and may cause irritability or sedation in the infant.
renal: Use with caution; no well-defined dose adjustment is established. Reduce dose if excess sedation occurs.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment, as metabolism may be reduced and sedative effects prolonged.

pearls: Not independently FDA-approved as a systemic single agent in the US; widely used elsewhere and in US combination/ophthalmic products (data from BNF/EMA/regional labels rather than a standalone US FDA label)
First-generation antihistamine - sedating and anticholinergic; caution in elderly and children
Injectable form is an adjunct in anaphylaxis - adrenaline remains first-line, not a substitute
Discontinue before allergy skin testing to avoid false-negative results
Avoid with alcohol and other CNS depressants
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and continue your usual schedule - do not take a double dose. For as-needed allergy use, take only when symptoms are present.
overdose: Overdose causes CNS depression (or paradoxical excitation/seizures in children), pronounced anticholinergic effects (dilated pupils, flushing, fever, dry mouth, tachycardia, urinary retention), and in severe cases coma and cardiorespiratory collapse. Management is supportive with airway protection, control of seizures and hyperthermia, and cardiac monitoring; there is no specific antidote (physostigmine only in select cases).
